questions.stem: A government passes a law to stop private companies from polluting a town's water supply. Which state obligation does this fulfill?
questions.explanation: Protect = preventing third parties from interfering with the right. B: Respect = the state itself not interfering. C: Fulfil = adopting measures to realize the right (e.g., building water systems). D, E: Not obligation levels.

questions.stem: Which international treaty article contains the most detailed provision on the right to health?
questions.explanation: ICESCR includes the most detailed provision: Article 12.1, the right to the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health. A: UDHR 25.1 is the right to a standard of living adequate for health (food, clothing, housing, medical care). B, C, E: Right-to-health provisions limited to specific populations (persons with disabilities, children, women).

questions.stem: A state signed a human-rights treaty but hasn't ratified it. What is its legal position?

options.A: Fully bound by every provision, as if ratified
options.B: Not bound, but must not undermine the treaty's purpose
options.C: Not bound, and free to act against its aims
options.D: Bound only to the treaty's minimum core obligations
options.E: A full party, as with accession

questions.explanation: Signature is a preliminary endorsement: no binding legal obligation, but the State must refrain from acts that undermine the treaty's object and purpose. A, D: Only ratification or accession creates binding obligations. C: Signature still carries the duty not to undermine the treaty. E: Accession makes a State a full party (same effect as ratification); signature alone does not.

questions.stem: According to the lecture, what distinguishes harm reduction for people who use drugs?

options.A: It requires abstinence before services are offered
options.B: It relies on criminal penalties to deter use
options.C: It serves only people already in drug treatment
options.D: It puts legal outcomes ahead of health outcomes
options.E: It does not necessarily require abstinence

questions.explanation: Harm reduction is evidence-based policy and practice that minimizes the health, social and legal harms of drug use and protects rights, without necessarily requiring abstinence, meeting people 'where they are'. A, C: It doesn't require abstinence or prior treatment. B: Criminalization drives unsafe injecting. D: It focuses on improving health outcomes.

questions.stem: A country cannot build a national primary-care network immediately because of limited resources, but it expands coverage every year toward measurable targets. Which ICESCR concept allows this?
questions.explanation: Progressive realization recognizes resource constraints and that the right to health can't be achieved immediately, but requires States to move as expeditiously and effectively as possible, tracked with indicators and benchmarks. A: The minimum core is what all States are obligated to implement, not a time allowance. B: Specific essential services (e.g., immunization, maternal care), not a timeline. D: A way of joining a treaty. E: Refraining from interfering with the right.

questions.stem: Which item is part of the minimum core obligations of the right to health, rather than the ICESCR priority obligations?

options.B: Provision of essential drugs as defined by the WHO
options.C: Reproductive, maternal and child health care
options.E: Education on the main health problems

questions.explanation: Minimum core: non-discriminatory access, minimum safe food, basic shelter, sanitation and water, essential drugs (WHO), equitable distribution, and a national public health strategy. A, C, D, E: Priority obligations listed by the ICESCR in addition to the core.

questions.stem: A State that took no part in negotiating or signing a treaty later becomes a party after the treaty has entered into force. What is this called, and what is its effect?

options.C: Accession; same legal effect as ratification
options.E: Reservation; binding only for chosen articles

questions.explanation: Accession is accepting the opportunity to join a treaty already negotiated and signed by others, usually after it enters into force; it has the same legal effect as ratification. A: Signature is only a preliminary endorsement. B: Ratification follows the State's own prior signature. D: Accession is not weaker. E: Reservations are not covered in the lecture.
